description: Details pursuant to the discharge of Condition 4 (Energy Strategy), 5 (Arboricultural Method Statement ), 8 (Archaeology), and 9 (Refuse and Recycling Management Plan) as attached to Appeal permission ref. APP/R5510/W/23/3327482 dated 15.05.2025 (planning application ref. 43794/APP/2021/3685) (Erection of a hotel and associated access, parking, landscaping and refuse storage).
application_type_full: Approval of details reserved by a condition (discharge)
decision_conditions: Insufficient information has been submitted to satisfy the requirements of Condition 4 (Energy Strategy) as attached to Appeal ref. APP/R5510/W/23/3327482 dated 15/05/2024 (Planning Application ref. 43794/APP/2021/3685 dated 21/03/2023). The submitted Energy Strategy fails to provide a clear and coordinated specification for the proposed heating, hot-water, ventilation and cooling systems, supported by appropriate non-domestic energy calculations for the approved 157-bedroom hotel. It also fails to provide a clear and verifiable assessment of the carbon reductions achieved at each stage of the energy hierarchy or adequately demonstrate that opportunities to minimise energy demand and maximise on-site carbon savings have been secured. The Local Planning Authority is therefore unable to confirm that the proposed energy measures are technically deliverable or would secure an appropriate level of on-site carbon reduction, contrary to Policy DMEI 2 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 (2020

Insufficient information has been submitted to satisfy the requirements of Condition 5 (Arboricultural Method Statement) as attached to Appeal ref. APP/R5510/W/23/3327482 dated 15/05/2024 (Planning Application ref. 43794/APP/2021/3685 dated 21/03/2023). The information submitted fails to demonstrate, through a sufficiently clear, current and site-specific Arboricultural Method Statement and Tree Protection Plan, that all trees shown for retention on approved plan TRP_242BATHRD_2 (Rev D) H would be fully safeguarded by appropriate protective fencing and ground protection during site clearance and construction. The submission also fails to resolve uncertainty regarding potential tree removal and works within the root protection areas of retained trees. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policy DMHB 14 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 (2020), Policy G7 of the London Plan (2021) and the National Planning Policy Framework. The application is therefore refused.

Insufficient information has been submitted to satisfy the requirements of Condition 8 (Archaeology) as attached to Appeal ref. APP/R5510/W/23/3327482 dated 15/05/2024 (Planning Application ref. 43794/APP/2021/3685 dated 21/03/2023). The information submitted fails to secure an appropriate programme of archaeological recording because a suitable Written Scheme of Investigation, including detailed arrangements for archaeological field evaluation, recording, reporting, archiving and any necessary subsequent mitigation, has not been submitted. The Local Planning Authority is therefore unable to ensure that archaeological remains would be appropriately investigated, recorded and safeguarded before development, including site-clearance works, commences. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policy DMHB 7 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 (2020), Policy HC1 of the London Plan (2021) and the National Planning Policy Framework. The application is therefore refused.

Insufficient information has been submitted to satisfy the requirements of Condition 9 (Refuse and Recycling Management Plan) as attached to Appeal ref. APP/R5510/W/23/3327482 dated 15/05/2024 (Planning Application ref. 43794/APP/2021/3685 dated 21/03/2023). The information submitted fails to provide a defined collection schedule or clearly identify the required refuse-vehicle reversing distance. The proposed container pull distance of approximately 21 metres has not been demonstrated to provide a safe and practicable collection arrangement, and the submission fails to demonstrate that sufficient provision has been made for food waste, recycling and general waste or satisfactorily assess the effect of the development on the existing refuse facilities serving Axis House. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies DMHB 11, DMT 1 and DMT 7 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 (2020), Policies SI 7 and T7 of the London Plan (2021) and the National Planning Policy Framework.
